description: Maintenance Mode - Admin can enable/disable maintenance mode via Settings. When enabled, non-admin users see a maintenance message and cannot use the bot. Admin panel continues to work normally.
steps: Add 'maintenance_mode' (default false/0) and 'maintenance_message' (default 'Bot is under maintenance. Please try again later.') to _DEFAULT_SETTINGS dict at line ~880.

Add two entries to SETTINGS_MAP: _b('🔧 Maintenance Mode') mapped to ('maintenance_mode', str, 'Enter ON or OFF:') and _b('🔧 Maintenance Msg') mapped to ('maintenance_message', str, 'Enter maintenance message text:').

Add maintenance mode check in AuthMiddleware.__call__ (line ~2312): After the banned check and before force-join check, if settings.maintenance_mode is truthy (value 'ON' or 1 or True) and user is not admin, respond with the maintenance_message and return (block processing). Cache settings briefly to avoid DB call per message - use a module-level variable _maintenance_cache with a TTL of 30 seconds.
Add special validation in receive_setting handler (line ~6850): when key is 'maintenance_mode', normalize input to 'ON' or 'OFF' string (accept case-insensitive on/off/1/0/true/false).
Show maintenance status in fmt_settings output: add a line showing current maintenance mode status (ON/OFF).
acceptance_criteria: python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('bot.py').read())" passes without errors
AuthMiddleware blocks non-admin users when maintenance_mode is ON
Admin can toggle maintenance via Settings menu
verification: python3 -c "exec(open('bot.py').read().split('if __name__')[0]); s = dict(_DEFAULT_SETTINGS); assert 'maintenance_mode' in s; assert 'maintenance_message' in s; print('Maintenance settings OK')"
